mainTopic: The four New Years of the opening משנה, and the גמרא's explanation of why kings need a fixed New Year (dating documents) and how their years are counted from ניסן.
overview: This amud opens מסכת ראש השנה with a משנה that lists four separate 'new year' dates, each for a different area of הלכה. א' ניסן is for kings and the order of the רגלים. א' אלול is for מעשר בהמה, though רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say א' תשרי. א' תשרי is for years, שמיטה, יובל, planting and vegetables. The new year for trees is א' שבט according to בית שמאי and ט"ו בשבט according to בית הלל. The גמרא then asks why kings need a new year at all, and רב חסדא answers that it matters for dating documents, since early-dated loan documents are invalid. A ברייתא shows how royal years turn over on א' ניסן, so that even one day of rule before ניסן counts as a full year. The גמרא re-quotes that line to draw a lesson from it, and the lesson itself comes on the next amud.

steps.title: There are four New Years, and the first is ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The משנה announces that there are four New Year dates. The first is א' ניסן, the new year for kings and for the order of the festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four New Years. On the first of ניסן is the New Year for kings and for the festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a headline: the calendar has four different 'new year' dates. It then gives the first one, א' ניסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'ראש השנה' here is a cut-off date for counting or grouping years in one specific area of הלכה. On א' ניסן a king's reign is counted as moving into its next year. ניסן also decides which festival counts as the first of the year's רגלים, so פסח comes first.

keyTerms.meaning: New Years (plural of רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה)
The spring month in which פסח falls
Kings; refers to counting the years of a king's reign
The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume 'ראש השנה' only means the holiday in תשרי. In this משנה the phrase means a starting point for counting years, and different areas of הלכה use different starting points.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list frames the whole first פרק. The גמרא will go through each item and ask what it means and where it comes from.

phrases.english: There are four New Years:
On the first of Nisan
is the New Year for kings and for the festivals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of the מסכת; no previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four New Year dates. א' ניסן is the New Year for counting kings' reigns and for the order of the רגלים.

steps.title: The first of אלול is the New Year for animal tithes
steps.stepSummary: The anonymous opinion (תנא קמא) gives א' אלול as the cut-off date for מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of אלול is the New Year for the tithe of animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second date: א' אלול is the new year for tithing animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With מעשר בהמה, every tenth animal born is set aside as holy. Animals born before the cut-off date cannot be counted together with animals born after it. According to this first opinion, that cut-off date is א' אלול.

keyTerms.meaning: The month just before תשרי
The tithe of animals: every tenth newborn animal is sanctified

phrases.english: On the first of Elul
is the New Year for animal tithes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list with the second New Year date.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, א' אלול is the New Year for מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say animal tithes start in תשרי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון disagree with the anonymous opinion. They hold that the New Year for מעשר בהמה is א' תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: on the first of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: Two named תנאים disagree with the previous line. They move the animal-tithe new year from אלול to תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic stays the same: the cut-off date for מעשר בהמה. Only the date changes. On their view, animal tithes share the same date as many other items on the list, which raises the question of how the משנה can still count four distinct new years. The גמרא deals with this later.

keyTerms.meaning: Say; the standard formula introducing a dissenting opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
On the first of Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the date given in step 2 for מעשר בהמה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the New Year for מעשר בהמה is א' תשרי.

steps.title: The first of תשרי is the New Year for years, שמיטה, יובל, planting and vegetables
steps.stepSummary: א' תשרי is the New Year for several things: counting years, שמיטה and יובל, planting (for ערלה), and tithing vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of תשרי is the New Year for years, for שמיטה years and יובל years, for planting, and for vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third date, א' תשרי. It covers the longest list of uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Years' is a general category, which the גמרא will explain. For שמיטה and יובל, working the land becomes forbidden from א' תשרי. 'Planting' refers to counting the three years of ערלה for a new tree. 'Vegetables' means vegetables picked before and after this date cannot be tithed together.

keyTerms.meaning: The autumn month in which the holiday of ראש השנה falls
Sabbatical years, every seventh year, when the land rests
Jubilee years, every fiftieth year
Planting; used for counting the years of עָרְלָה
Vegetables; refers to tithing them

steps.confusionAlert: Although one date covers many uses here, the משנה still counts תשרי as just one of the four New Years. The count is of dates, not of uses.

phrases.english: On the first of Tishrei
is the New Year for years,
and for Sabbatical Years and Jubilee Years,
for planting and for vegetables.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main list after the dispute and gives the third New Year date.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: א' תשרי is the New Year for years, שמיטה, יובל, planting (ערלה), and tithing vegetables.

steps.title: The first of שבט is the New Year for trees, according to בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The fourth date is א' שבט, the New Year for trees. The משנה says this follows the view of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of שבט is the New Year for the tree, according to the words of בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its fourth date, the new year for trees. It tells us right away that this is בית שמאי's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This date affects tithing fruit. Fruit that formed before the date belongs to the previous year and cannot be tithed together with fruit that formed after it. Labeling the date as בית שמאי's sets up the dispute in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: The winter month after טבת
Tree; refers to tithing tree fruit
According to the words of

phrases.english: On the first of Shevat
is the New Year for the tree,
according to the words of Beit Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fourth and final New Year date.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, א' שבט is the New Year for trees.

steps.title: בית הלל say the New Year for trees is the fifteenth of שבט
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל disagree with בית שמאי and put the New Year for trees on ט"ו בשבט. The הלכה follows בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: on the fifteenth of it (שבט).
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל disagree with the date from the previous line. They say the new year for trees is two weeks later, on the fifteenth of שבט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בּוֹ' ('of it') refers back to שבט, so both sides agree on the month and disagree only on the day. This is the source of the date we know as ט"ו בשבט.

keyTerms.meaning: Fifteen; the fifteenth day
Of it; refers back to the month שבט

steps.whatToRemember: The four New Years: א' ניסן (kings, festivals). א' אלול (animal tithes; רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say תשרי). א' תשרי (years, שמיטה, יובל, planting, vegetables). שבט for trees (בית שמאי say the 1st, בית הלל say the 15th, and the הלכה follows בית הלל).
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, ט"ו בשבט became the date that is still marked today.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel say:
On the fifteenth of it (Shevat).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the date for trees given in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, the New Year for trees is ט"ו בשבט.

steps.title: Why do kings need a New Year?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what practical law depends on the משנה's 'New Year for kings.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The New Year 'for kings': what law does it matter for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the משנה. It asks what practical difference the 'New Year for kings' makes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other New Years in the משנה clearly matter for הלכה, such as מעשר, שמיטה and ערלה. Counting a king's years seems to be only history, not הלכה. So the גמרא asks what הלכה actually depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion that explains the משנה
For kings, meaning counting the years of a king's rule
For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: Gemara: 'For kings':
for what law is this needed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of dates in the משנה and starts the גמרא's explanation, beginning with the first item, kings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical הלכה depends on having a fixed New Year for counting a king's reign.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it matters for documents
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that the king's New Year matters for dating legal documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It matters for documents.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The king's New Year matters for legal documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Documents were dated by the year of the king's reign, for example 'year 3 of King X.' To know the true date written on a document, everyone has to agree on when each royal year begins. So a fixed New Year for kings is needed to read dates correctly.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal documents, here mainly loan documents

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
For documents.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The fixed royal New Year is needed to date documents correctly.

steps.title: Early-dated loan documents are invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה showing why a document's exact date matters: early-dated loan documents are invalid, and late-dated ones are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Loan documents that are dated early are invalid, and those dated late are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to show why the date on a document is so important. This explains why רב חסדא's answer makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A loan document gives the lender a claim on the borrower's land from the date written on it. An early date would let the lender unfairly take land from buyers who bought it before the real loan, so such a document is invalid. A late date only hurts the lender himself, so it is valid. Since a document can be ruined by its date, everyone must know exactly when the king's year begins.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
Dated earlier than the actual loan
Dated later than the actual loan
Invalid / valid

steps.confusionAlert: Do not reverse the rule. The early-dated (מוקדם) document is the invalid one, because it can harm innocent buyers. The late-dated (מאוחר) one is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical reason the 'New Year for kings' is הלכה and not just history. A mistake about when the year starts could make a valid document look early-dated and invalid.

phrases.english: As we learned: loan documents that are dated early
are invalid, and those dated late are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's answer by showing that a document's date has real legal results.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the royal New Year matters for documents
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (שביעית פרק י' משנה ה') that early-dated loan documents are invalid and late-dated ones are valid

steps.title: A ברייתא: how a king's years are counted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a king who began ruling on כ"ט אדר finishes a year on א' ניסן. A king who began on א' ניסן only adds a year at the next ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A king who began ruling on the 29th of אדר: once א' ניסן arrives, a year is counted for him. But if he only began on א' ניסן, we do not count another year for him until the next ניסן comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that shows exactly how a king's years are counted. ניסן is the point where a new royal year begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even one day of rule before ניסן counts as a full first year, so on א' ניסן the king enters his second year. A king who begins on א' ניסן itself has a full year until the next ניסן. The count follows the calendar starting at ניסן, not the king's personal start date.

keyTerms.meaning: Rose to power, began to rule
A year is counted for him
We do not count

steps.confusionAlert: 'A year is counted' means his first year is finished on א' ניסן and he enters year two. It does not mean his first year begins then.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A king who began ruling on the 29th of Adar,
once the first of Nisan arrives,
a year is counted for him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לֹא עָמַד אֶלָּא בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן —
phrases.english: But if he only began ruling on the first of Nisan,
we do not count a year for him
until the next Nisan arrives.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶלֶךְ שֶׁעָמַד בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בַּאֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from why the royal New Year matters to how it works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Royal years turn over on א' ניסן. Even one day of rule before ניסן counts as a full year.

steps.title: Re-quoting the ברייתא to draw a lesson
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first half of the ברייתא again and begins with 'הא' ('this teaches...') to draw a lesson from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: A king who began ruling on the 29th of אדר: once א' ניסן arrives, a year is counted for him. This...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the first ruling of the ברייתא on purpose. This is a setup line: with the word 'הא' it is about to explain what this ruling teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repetition has a real purpose. The גמרא wants to pull lessons from this line, for example that ניסן is the New Year for kings and that one day of a year counts as a whole year. This passage stops right as that lesson begins.

keyTerms.meaning: This, which introduces a lesson drawn from the quoted text

phrases.english: The Master said:
A king who began ruling on the 29th of Adar,
once the first of Nisan arrives,
a year is counted for him.
This...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, where the גמרא explains what the line teaches.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מֶלֶךְ שֶׁעָמַד בְּעֶשְׂרִים וְתִשְׁעָה בַּאֲדָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes part of the ברייתא from step 10 in order to analyze it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a lesson drawn from the ruling that one day before ניסן counts as a full royal year.
